channel.title: AgentScout
channel.description: Latest AI agent tools and agent news from AgentScout.

item.title: Kurodyne
item.description: Kurodyne is a marketplace of skills, prompts, automation workflows, software tools, spreadsheets and templates that AI agents can search. Its Catalog MCP server is free to use with no account, so agents can search products, read reviews and pull each product's README. Sellers use a separate Seller Console MCP to have their own agent publish products and answer buyers. Prices run from $5 to $500, with a 20% fee per sale and no listing or monthly fees. A person reviews every listing, and packages are malware-scanned and fingerprinted.

item.title: Microsoft Agent Skills
item.description: Microsoft Agent Skills is an MIT collection of skills, custom agents, AGENTS.md templates and MCP configuration for coding agents that use Azure SDKs and Microsoft AI Foundry. The README says the repo is still in progress and that the skill explorer lists 175 skills. Install is npx skills add microsoft/skills. The explorer at https://microsoft.github.io/skills/ returned HTTP 200 on 27 Nov 2026. GitHub microsoft/skills showed 3,255 stars and 376 forks that day.

item.title: Agent Toolkit for AWS
item.description: The Agent Toolkit for AWS gives coding agents tools, knowledge and guardrails for building on AWS. The README says it works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Kiro and fx, and that the AWS CLI command is aws configure agent-toolkit. The CLI guide at that docs URL returned HTTP 200 on 27 Nov 2026. Plugins also install from Anthropic's Claude Code marketplace, including an aws-core plugin. GitHub aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws recorded Apache-2.0, 3,594 stars and 487 forks on 27 Nov 2026. The README did not list a separate toolkit price.

item.title: Laravel Boost
item.description: Laravel Boost is an MIT package that gives a coding agent Laravel-specific context so the code it writes matches a Laravel app. The README points documentation at the Laravel site. That docs page returned HTTP 200 on 27 Nov 2026 at https://laravel.com/framework/docs/13.x/boost. Release v2.10.4 was published 29 Oct 2026 and adds a command to re-index rules. GitHub laravel/boost showed 3,697 stars and 393 forks on 27 Nov 2026.

item.title: OpenGame
item.description: OpenGame is an Apache-2.0 game studio for coding agents. The README calls it a full-stack agent that remixes, restyles, tests and publishes playable 3D, anime, pixel and vertical mini-games, and it says the repo includes 25 playable templates and 22 local agents. GitHub nexu-io/opengame showed 1,799 stars and 295 forks on 27 Nov 2026. The repo has no homepage of its own. It is a different repository from nexu-io/html-video and nexu-io/html-anything.

item.title: Simlock
item.description: Simlock leases iOS simulators, Android emulators and enrolled phones to coding agents so two agents do not use the same device at once. The site on 27 Nov 2026 says it is free and open source, that one Mac is enough to start, and that more machines can sit behind a gateway. Install is npm i -g simlock. Release v0.9.0, published 26 Nov 2026, requires agent-device 0.21.40 or later on every worker. This listing is Simlock, not Agent Device. GitHub callstackincubator/simlock recorded MIT, 727 stars and 42 forks on 27 Nov 2026.

item.title: Freebuff
item.description: Freebuff is an Apache-2.0 coding agent from Codebuff. The README says there is no subscription, no credits and no API key, and that text ads pay for the included models. It names four products: a desktop app that runs agents locally, a CLI, a web builder for full-stack apps, and a cloud runner for GitHub repositories. GitHub CodebuffAI/freebuff showed 14,336 stars and 1,551 forks on 27 Nov 2026.

item.title: Kaeso
item.description: Kaeso is a self-hosted AI gateway in Rust. The homepage on 27 Nov 2026 says apps call one API while provider keys stay on the gateway, encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a master key you hold, and that a hard budget can refuse a request before any provider is called. The page showed version 0.7.4 and said that release stops a CPU-heavy merge of a tool schema after 4,096 schemas. Docs include an MCP portal at https://docs.kaeso.app/concepts/mcp-portal. GitHub logicplanes/kaeso recorded MIT, 62 stars and 3 forks on 27 Nov 2026. The homepage sample prices are pass-through provider rates in the demo console, not a Kaeso subscription.

item.title: Pepys
item.description: Pepys Transcribe turns audio and video into timestamped text, and ships a hosted MCP server so an agent can transcribe on its own. The MCP docs on 27 Nov 2026 say the server is https://pepys.co/api/mcp, sign-in is OAuth, and the server is listed in Claude's connector directory. A POST initialize without an authorization header returned HTTP 401. The pricing page said the first 60 minutes are free with no card. After that, audio is $1.25 an hour on purchases under $20, $1.00 an hour from $20, and $0.85 an hour from $85. One credit is one minute, credits do not expire, and speaker labels use 1.5 credits a minute. The docs named a separate stdio package at https://github.com/ankurmans/pepys-mcp. GitHub showed that repo at MIT, 0 stars and 0 forks on 27 Nov 2026.

item.title: MotifDeck
item.description: MotifDeck makes 2D game characters, sprites and short animations, then exports sprite sheets. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 listed Free at $0 with 60 welcome credits that do not expire. Starter was $19 a month for 1,500 credits, Creator $39 for 3,600, Pro $79 for 8,500 and Studio $159 for 20,000. Annual billing was shown as 25% less. The page says the credit cost is shown before a run. Free includes a limited number of tool runs. This is a game-art workspace, not a general image chat.

item.title: We0
item.description: We0 generates a website or app with payments, login and an admin, using a multi-agent build and a visual canvas. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 listed Free at $0 with one full generation and 100 credits on sign-up. Plus was shown as $29 crossed out and $18 a month, with 888 credits. Pro was shown as $286 crossed out and $240 a year, with 12,888 credits. The page said one project usually costs about 60 to 150 credits, a standard step 3 to 6 credits and a complex step 6 to 20. The public content index is linked from that page at https://we0.ai/llms.txt.

item.title: KOMA
item.description: KOMA, from Alchemint, turns a line, a script or reference media into a storyboard and a video, and the homepage also describes a CLI that tells a local AI which shots to move or generate. The homepage on 27 Nov 2026 listed a one-time pack at US$10 for 1,000 credits, and monthly plans from US$10 a month. Lite includes 1,000 credits each month plus 100 image-01 images. The page says each generation spends credits based on the model and settings. Named models on the page included Seedance 2.5 and MiniMax H3. The page did not show a $0 plan.

item.title: Ofox Chat
item.description: Ofox is one OpenAI-compatible API for many chat, image and video models, aimed at coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Cline. The homepage on 27 Nov 2026 said Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi start at $0.3 per million tokens, images start at $0.03 an image, and video starts at $2.1 per million tokens. The page also showed a desktop app that connects those coding tools. No public source repository was checked for this listing, so the pricing label follows the per-token prices on the page.

item.title: SongDuet
item.description: SongDuet generates songs with more than one music model and then splits stems, MIDI and sheet music. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 said a free account gets 20 credits to try the SongDuet model and listen online. Starter was $9.99 a month or $7.99 with the annual price shown, with 500 credits and up to 100 songs a month. Creator was $29.99 or $14.99 on that annual display, with 2,000 credits and up to 400 songs. Studio was $59.99 or $39.99, with 5,000 credits and up to 1,000 songs. Paid plans include the named models (Google Lyria, ElevenLabs Music, MiniMax, Mureka and open models) and a commercial license. Monthly credits reset.

item.title: PennyCompute
item.description: PennyCompute generates video with MiniMax H3 and renders footage with FFmpeg. The homepage on 27 Nov 2026 priced a MiniMax H3 clip at $0.025 for five seconds at 480p fast quality, with optional first frame, last frame or reference files. The rendering list covered transcode, stitch, mix audio, burn subtitles, export a timeline, grab frames and make a sound file. The MCP docs say the server is https://api.pennycompute.com/mcp and that initialize, tools/list and ping work without an API key. Job calls need a PennyCompute server key.

item.title: Sandscale
item.description: Sandscale runs Firecracker microVM sandboxes, workspaces and build machines for AI agents. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 listed a free plan at $0 a month with 100 awake vCPU-hours, 3 concurrent sandboxes, 5 GB of storage and one workspace. Pro was $20 a month billed annually or $25 billed monthly, with 1,500 awake vCPU-hours. Team was $40 per member a month annually or $48 monthly, with 2,000 awake vCPU-hours per member. Usage past the hours was $0.05 per awake vCPU-hour, hour packs were $10 per 500 hours, and storage past the allowance was $0.15 per GB-month. The first 10 GB of storage was free. The docs tell Claude Code to connect to https://mcp.sandscale.dev/mcp. A POST initialize without a session on 27 Nov 2026 returned HTTP 401 and asked the caller to sign in.

item.title: Idol Max
item.description: Idol Max turns one image into a GLB 3D model with UVs and a 2K texture. The homepage on 27 Nov 2026 priced Idol Max Turbo at 10 credits (about 20 seconds) and Idol Max at 20 credits (about 50 seconds). A rig add-on was +3 credits on Turbo and +5 on Idol Max, and PBR maps were +10. Failed generations are refunded. The page says the image is sent to fal.ai to build the model. The GLB viewer and turntable export are free and do not spend credits. Credit packs were $10 for 400 credits, $25 for 1,250, $50 for 3,000 and $100 for 7,000, and the page says credits never expire.

item.title: KDPBook
item.description: KDPBook plans, writes, illustrates and typesets a book for Amazon KDP upload. The site says it is not affiliated with Amazon. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 listed Free at $0 with 1,000 welcome credits and no card, Starter at $19 a month for 2,500 credits, Author at $39 for 5,500 and Studio at $79 for 12,000. Yearly billing was shown as 20% less. One-time packs were 1,200 credits for $12 and 3,000 for $29. The page's examples at default settings were about 1,013 credits for a 32-page illustrated picture book, 765 for a 50-design coloring book and 1,165 for a 50,000-word novel with a cover. It says a failed step is not charged and paid plans include commercial rights.

item.title: BlendCanvas
item.description: BlendCanvas is an infinite canvas for AI images and video. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 listed a free trial at $0 with 10 welcome credits for a new verified account, Starter at $12 a month for 1,000 credits, Creator at $24 for 2,100 and Studio at $49 for 4,500. One-time packs were $5 for 500 credits, $10 for 1,000 and $25 for 2,500. The same page said paid subscriptions were not open yet, and that a failed generation refunds the reserved credits. The MCP page documents https://app.blendcanvas.com/api/mcp and said remote MCP was currently unavailable for that workspace.

item.title: Skillbox
item.description: Skillbox keeps a library of AI skills and syncs them across the tools a person already uses. The homepage on 27 Nov 2026 says you can paste a GitHub URL, a README command or an owner/repo, and that sync stays off until you turn it on. The pricing page listed Free at £0 a month (up to 3 devices and 100 followed sources), Individual at £6.99 a month after a 7-day trial, and Team at £12.99 per active member a month. Free needs no card. Individual adds context trim and Skillbox AI and removes the device and source caps.

item.title: Switzerland says AI agents broke into four of five targets
item.description: The Next Web reports that Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre has five confirmed cases of cyberattacks carried out with AI agents, and that attackers got into systems in four of them. Director Florian Schütz told SRF on Thursday that three cases targeted critical-infrastructure operators and two of those succeeded, with no major outages. The centre's Tuesday notice had said every known case succeeded. It wants critical updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours, and multi-factor authentication or passkeys on services such as webmail and VPNs.

item.title: Papa John's order is the UK's first cardless AI agent payment
item.description: The Guardian reports that an order of nine Papa John's mini pizzas is the first UK purchase in which an AI agent paid a retailer without a card. The Financial Conduct Authority sandbox trial used Lloyds Bank and TrueLayer. The agent had a spend cap per transaction and per month, and no account security details were shared. TrueLayer chief executive Francesco Simoneschi said the customer described the occasion, confirmed the order, and existing buyer-protection rules still apply if the agent orders the wrong thing.

item.title: Black Friday tests shopping agents, and most shoppers will not let them pay
item.description: Fortune reports that a Morning Consult poll for Visa found 54 percent of adults have used AI for at least one shopping task, while 23 percent trust generative AI to handle a payment. In a Visa trial, 22 personal agents shopped for a TV, a laptop, and a hair appliance, and only 57 percent of 15 trips each ended in a suitable purchase or suggestion. An American Express survey found 52 percent would let an agent buy low-cost essentials, and 15 percent would let it buy big-ticket electronics.

item.title: Mail opens an MCP server for email, cloud files, and calendar
item.description: VK's Mail opened an MCP server on 27 November 2026 so an AI agent can work in Mail, Cloud, and Calendar for every user. In mail it can find messages and attachments, summarize a thread, and draft or send mail. In cloud storage it can upload, download, and sort files. In the calendar it can find a free time, create an event from a message, and add a call link. The server only sees what that user can already see, and the person signs in and chooses what to allow.

item.title: UK retailers ask who pays if a shopping agent gets the order wrong
item.description: The Guardian reports that Meta's Muse, which launched in the UK on Tuesday, is working with Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's, JD Sports, and Currys. A YouGov poll found a third of people planning to shop Black Friday intend to get help from AI, up from 19 percent last year, while KPMG found 12 percent plan to use an AI tool specifically to find deals. Muse must ask before it buys or sends email. Retailers told the paper they will not hand over checkout until it is clear who is liable when an agent gets an order wrong.

item.title: Linux 7.5 is set to gain in-tree skills for coding agents
item.description: Phoronix reports that NVIDIA's Sasha Levin, who co-maintains the Linux long-term kernels, plans to send an agents/skills directory to Linus Torvalds for the Linux 7.5 merge window in late December. He asked for the branch to be dropped from linux-next because it is ready for mainline. The first skills cover Fixes tags, stable tags, finding other copies of a bug, commit messages, and KUnit tests.

item.title: Enhancv opens a resume MCP server inside Claude and ChatGPT
item.description: Enhancv launched a remote MCP server on 26 November 2026 that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code edit the resume stored in a person's Enhancv account. Changes show up in the editor to keep or undo, and the connector is told to ask when a bullet needs a number the person has not given. It cannot delete resumes or reach billing. Reading and job search work on the free plan. Editing, tailoring, cover letters, and PDF downloads need Enhancv Pro.

item.title: Meta declined a UK watchdog's offer to test Muse before launch
item.description: WIRED reports that Meta turned down a Financial Conduct Authority suggestion to test Muse together in the regulator's sandbox before the UK rollout. Colin Payne, the FCA's head of innovation, said the agency wants to see how the agent handles payments and whether it acts for the customer. Meta said it has engaged with the relevant regulators. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will act if it has concerns about UK consumers.

item.title: Gap uses Cognition's Devin to keep holiday shopping online
item.description: Gap Inc. said on 25 November 2026 that engineers use Cognition's Devin agent on its ecommerce sites. A daily site scan looks for shopper friction and system faults, then drafts a tested code fix for a person to review and publish. Gap says that work has helped recover millions in sales that downtime would have lost, and that people still approve every change.

item.title: Human Security sees AI agent traffic heading for a 150x Cyber Week
item.description: Adweek reports that Human Security expects AI agent traffic during Cyber Week, 26 to 30 November, to reach about 150 times last year's level, with checkout-page requests near 160 times. Meta's Muse accounts for about 70 percent of the agent traffic Human sees and 57 percent of checkout requests. The figures count page and search actions on sites Human protects, not completed orders.

item.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
item.description: TechCrunch reports that Amazon and Meta have held talks about letting Muse shop on Amazon, according to Fortune. The open questions are how search results would appear and how advertising would work, and any deal would need both chief executives to approve it. Two months ago, Muse shoppers could not check out on Amazon. Neither company had commented.

item.title: Duco opens an MCP server for post-trade reconciliation agents
item.description: Duco made its MCP server generally available on 25 November 2026. Agents on any MCP client can search reconciliation breaks, label them, and match or clear exceptions under the user's existing permissions. Every action is written to Duco's audit log, and the server is available to Duco clients.

item.title: Alta opens an MCP server so sales agents can prospect in chat
item.description: Alta opened Alta MCP in Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex on 25 November 2026. A rep can describe an audience, get verified contacts, and draft a multichannel campaign in the same chat. Campaigns stay drafts until a person launches them, and sending or resuming a campaign asks for confirmation first.

item.title: Magister opens a marketing MCP server across 85 tools
item.description: Magister Marketing launched an MCP server on 25 November 2026 that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients to 85 marketing tools. It can read analytics and ad accounts and draft posts, but anything that publishes, sends, or spends waits for a person to approve it. Connect is $29 a month and the Agent plan is $99 a month, after a free trial.

item.title: Google Workspace opens MCP servers and a CLI for governed AI agents
item.description: Google made Workspace MCP servers and a Workspace CLI generally available, giving agents a managed way into Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace apps. A new addendum tells agents to use those doors instead of REST APIs, with technical enforcement starting 1 February 2027. Admins can require confirmations, read audit logs, and revoke access.

item.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
item.description: TechCrunch covers ShellBench, a test of 100 everyday tasks built from real agent requests in messy personal files. The leading models finished only about 60 percent of attempts, and 15.7 percent of all runs missed a safety check. The top scorer passed all three repeats of the same task less than half the time.

item.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
item.description: TechCrunch reports Walmart is partnering with Meta so Black Friday deals show up inside Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

item.title: Maple raises $5.3M for a private desktop agent and a cloud agent that stays on
item.description: TechCrunch reports Maple closed a $5.3 million seed round led by Epic Ventures. Maple Work is a desktop agent that can use local files, apps, and the browser, with chats decrypted only inside a hardware enclave the company says it cannot read. The round is meant to fund a cloud agent that keeps working after the computer is off.

item.title: Anthropic opens Skills over MCP and long-running tasks in Claude
item.description: Anthropic put Skills over MCP in public beta, so apps connected to Claude can ship step-by-step guides that load only when a task needs them. Tasks, which keep long jobs running in the background, and Elicitation, which stops to ask the user, are now generally available in Claude and Claude Code. Shopify, GitHub, and Supabase are among the first users.

item.title: JFrog says an AI agent published Hugging Face malware and leaked its own keys
item.description: JFrog Security Research says an autonomous agent it calls ARTEX uploaded fake Hugging Face models that steal cloud credentials and commit them back to a public repo. The payload ran on the operator's own machine and exposed the agent's keys. Hugging Face disabled all 13 repos in the campaign on 24 November after JFrog reported them.

item.title: Mesh launches an MCP server so coding agents can build payments flows
item.description: Mesh launched Mesh MCP, a hosted server that lets a coding agent assemble a payments integration from Mesh's live documentation and API spec. Each request is checked against that spec before it is sent. The server is read-only, does not move funds, and connects to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients.

item.title: UK ICO says it will act if consumer AI agents ship without user controls
item.description: The UK Information Commissioner's Office said it will step in when organisations rush out consumer AI agents without privacy safeguards and real user controls. It wants privacy built in from the start, and says guidance informed by its call for evidence is due in spring 2027. The post does not name a product or announce a fine.

item.title: OpenAI starts testing always-on Dots agents on the $20 Plus plan
item.description: The Verge reports OpenAI is testing its always-on Dots agents with a small number of $20 ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Dots had been limited to Pro and higher tiers, and they are also rolling out to every ChatGPT Business Standard user.

item.title: Kong says its Volcano agent cloud is live and looks for bugs on its own
item.description: Kong's November 19 post says Volcano, its agent cloud, is live: one place to host agents and apps, with sandboxes, durable workflows, and a system that finds bugs and proposes fixes. Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code can deploy to it.

item.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
item.description: Bloomberg found an Apple job listing for an AI agent that can browse, use apps, run commands, and write code on a Mac. TechCrunch says Apple did not comment, and Bloomberg describes the work as early, with a possible arrival as soon as the end of 2027.
